items.title: Huracán Isaías trae lluvia, viento y deja a miles de personas sin electricidad
items.author: Joe Wertz, Brian K. Sullivan
items.summary: Mientras los riesgos tropicales remiten en el este, el oeste de México y el suroeste de EE.UU. se enfrentan a una doble amenaza: la tormenta tropical Rachel y el huracán Simón.
items.body: Bloomberg — Las lluvias torrenciales se extenderán por el sur de Estados Unidos y los Apalaches mientras los remanentes del huracán Isaías avanzan hacia el norte, tras tocar tierra en Florida el viernes por la noche, dejando sin electricidad a cientos de miles de residentes en tres estados. Ver más: Huracán Isaías paraliza el 72% de la producción petrolera en el Golfo de EE.UU. Existe un riesgo moderado de lluvias intensas en algunas zonas del oeste de Carolina del Norte, hacia el sur hasta Georgia, este sábado, según ha informado el Centro de Predicción Meteorológica de EE.UU. La región quedó devastada cuando el huracán Helene arrasó la zona en 2024, provocando inundaciones en las ciudades, bloqueando carreteras y causando la muerte de al menos 249 personas en todo el país. Isaías no debería traer consigo la fuerza destructiva que desató Helene, según ha declarado Marc Chenard, meteorólogo jefe del Centro de Predicción Meteorológica de EE.UU. “Todavía tenemos que estar atentos a la zona sur de los Apalaches. Parece que allí podría haber algunos efectos significativos a lo largo del día”. Isaías pondrá a unas 12,6 millones de personas, desde Florida hasta Virginia, en riesgo de nivel dos por tormentas eléctricas severas, que pueden traer lluvias torrenciales y provocar tornados, durante todo el fin de semana, según ha informado el Centro de Predicción de Tormentas de EE.UU. La tormenta también afectó a la producción energética en todo el Golfo de México durante la semana y dejó sin suministro eléctrico a más de 875.000 hogares y empresas hasta el sábado por la mañana, según PowerOutage.com. La producción de petróleo en el Golfo de México se desplomó a medida que la tormenta se acercaba a la costa estadounidense; las empresas evacuaron a las tripulaciones de las plataformas como medida de precaución y las empresas de perforación alejaron las plataformas de su trayectoria. La tormenta de categoría 2 tocó tierra a las 20:30 horas cerca de Destin, Florida, con vientos máximos de 105 millas (169 kilómetros) por hora. Se degradó rápidamente a ciclón postropical, según el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de EE.UU. El primer huracán que azota Estados Unidos en casi dos años traerá lluvias generalizadas de hasta 8 pulgadas (20 centímetros) en toda la región, con precipitaciones de hasta 15 pulgadas en algunas zonas concretas. Según los meteorólogos, es probable que las condiciones de tormenta tropical continúen el sábado por la mañana, ya que el sistema tormentoso se desplazará hacia el norte a través de Alabama y se adentrará en los valles de Tennessee y Ohio a lo largo del día y hasta el domingo. Se prevé que el sistema tormentoso traiga lluvias intensas y que pueda generar tornados hasta en las Carolinas. Mientras los riesgos tropicales remiten en el este, el oeste de México y el suroeste de EE.UU. se enfrentan a una doble amenaza: la tormenta tropical Rachel y el huracán Simón. Se prevé que Rachel azote cerca de la frontera entre Estados Unidos y México, en el norte de Baja California, a última hora del sábado y que, a continuación, provoque lluvias torrenciales en todo el suroeste de Estados Unidos, incluidas partes de California, Arizona y Nevada, según ha informado el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos. Hay alertas de tormenta tropical, aunque poco frecuentes, en todo el sur de California, incluida San Diego. Más al sur, se prevé que Simón toque tierra cerca de Manzanillo (México), el puerto más activo del país en el Pacífico, durante la noche como huracán de categoría 4 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson de cinco niveles, con vientos de 155 millas por hora. Podrían caer hasta 20 pulgadas de lluvia en amplias zonas, con puntas aisladas de hasta 40 pulgadas. “Es probable que se produzcan vientos catastróficos y marejadas ciclónicas que pongan en peligro la vida a lo largo de una parte de la costa centro-occidental de México”, señaló el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de EE.UU. Las lluvias “provocarán inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que pondrán en peligro la vida”. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Abbas aplaza las elecciones palestinas y fija las presidenciales para septiembre de 2027
items.author: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: El presidente palestino, Mahmud Abás, aplazó el sábado las elecciones legislativas previstas para el próximo mes hasta el 11 de septiembre de 2027 y convocó unas elecciones presidenciales para esa misma fecha, achacando el retraso a Israel y a la situación de seguridad en los territorios palestinos.
items.body:
El presidente palestino, Mahmud Abás, aplazó el sábado las elecciones legislativas previstas para el próximo mes hasta el 11 de septiembre de 2027 y convocó unas elecciones presidenciales para esa misma fecha, achacando el retraso a Israel y a la situación de seguridad en los territorios palestinos.
El decreto de Abbas citaba "los obstáculos que plantean las medidas israelíes" y la necesidad de establecer unas condiciones políticas, de seguridad y sobre el terreno adecuadas para celebrar "elecciones libres, justas e inclusivas", informó la agencia oficial de noticias palestina WAFA.
El decreto instaba a los palestinos de Jerusalén, Cisjordania y Gaza a acudir a las urnas.
Existían serias dudas sobre si las elecciones de la Autoridad Palestina se celebrarían el próximo mes.
Los palestinos no han celebrado elecciones legislativas ni presidenciales desde 2005-2006, tras lo cual el rival de Abbas, el grupo islamista Hamás, tomó el control de Gaza, derrocando a sus partidarios.
Abbas ha gobernado por decreto desde que expiró su mandato presidencial en 2009.
El decreto señaló que los ataques militares israelíes, la expansión de los asentamientos, la violencia de los colonos y las restricciones de movimiento en Cisjordania, incluido Jerusalén Este, junto con la continua retención por parte de Israel de los ingresos fiscales palestinos, planteaban dificultades para la preparación y celebración de las elecciones de noviembre.
En Gaza, el decreto señalaba las "condiciones humanitarias y de seguridad excepcionales", la retirada incompleta de las fuerzas israelíes, la falta de avances en la reconstrucción y el incumplimiento de los acuerdos para el despliegue de fuerzas internacionales de estabilización y de policía.
Las restricciones israelíes al acceso del personal de la comisión electoral y de los observadores internacionales a Gaza y Jerusalén Este también complicaron los preparativos, según el decreto.
La decisión de aplazar las elecciones se tomó tras consultar con las facciones y fuerzas políticas palestinas. También tenía por objeto dar tiempo para que se lleve a cabo un diálogo nacional palestino exhaustivo con el fin de reforzar la unidad y abordar los retos a los que se enfrenta el proceso electoral.
Dos responsables palestinos dijeron el jueves a Reuters que los líderes del movimiento Fatah, de Abbas, y de su rival Hamás habían acordado en una reunión el miércoles en El Cairo aplazar las elecciones.
COMPROMISO CON ELECCIONES El aplazamiento se anuncia apenas unas semanas después de que Abbas reafirmó el calendario electoral de noviembre en su discurso del 24 de septiembre ante la Asamblea General de la ONU, en un intento por impulsar reformas respaldadas internacionalmente.
Abbas se había comprometido por escrito con el presidente francés Emmanuel Macron y con el príncipe heredero saudí Mohammed bin Salman a celebrar elecciones presidenciales y legislativas como parte del reconocimiento por parte de Francia de un Estado palestino en septiembre de 2025.
El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores francés dijo el jueves que la celebración de las elecciones era esencial y acogió con satisfacción la puesta en marcha de una misión de observación electoral de la UE.

By Timour Azhari and Enas Alashray
RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) – More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to Riyadh’s international airport and travellers were evacuated from parts of the facility after a loud blast was heard there on Saturday, an eyewitness and people briefed on the matter said.

Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this week, leaving four people dead and others wounded, and badly damaging an aircraft.

The Saudi government’s media office and the Saudi civil aviation authority did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the incident.

Show Full Article

Flight tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point.

The airport urged passengers to contact their airlines directly and check their flight status before heading there.

Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday.

Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host major energy and investment conferences.

Organisers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.

The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.

(Reporting by Timour Azhari in RiyadhWriting by Enas AlashrayEditing by Gareth Jones)

items.title: Augsburg score fastest Bundesliga goal but Bayern snatch comeback draw
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer scored after eight seconds of the game against visitors Bayern Munich on Saturday to record the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, but the German champions twice came from a goal down to snatch a 2-2 draw.
items.body:
Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer scored after eight seconds of the game against visitors Bayern Munich on Saturday to record the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, but the German champions twice came from a goal down to snatch a 2-2 draw.
Fellhauer benefited from a blunder by Bayern's Manuel Neuer as the keeper tried to clear but sent the ball to the Augsburg player who improved the record held jointly by Kevin Volland and Karim Bellarabi with goals after nine seconds.
The Bavarians, whose only league defeat in their last 48 matches was by Augsburg in January, upped their game after the break, having an effort ruled offside in the 51st before Ismael Saibari bagged the equaliser four minutes later.
It was another Neuer error that put Augsburg ahead again in the 64th minute, the 40-year-old punching Calvin Brackelmann's shot into the path of Rodrigo Ribeiro who only had to push the ball over the line.
Bayern battled back once more, however, when Harry Kane, who hit the woodwork in the first half, cut the ball back for Nathaniel Brown to tap in the equaliser 10 minutes from time.
Gnabry hit the post three minutes but Bayern had to settle for a point and second place on 11. Borussia Dortmund are top on 13 points.

items.title: Three injured in Poland's third youth stabbing attack in four days
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Three people were injured in a stabbing attack at a further education college in Warsaw on Saturday, police said, the latest in a series of incidents that have stoked concerns in Poland about copycat violence among young people.
items.body:
Three people were injured in a stabbing attack at a further education college in Warsaw on Saturday, police said, the latest in a series of incidents that have stoked concerns in Poland about copycat violence among young people.
On Friday [USN:L1N45V0E9 TEXT:"thousands of police"] visited schools nationwide to try to reassure pupils after two stabbing sprees by teenagers in as many days sparked rumours of potential further attacks, fears that Saturday's incident is likely to intensify.
"At 12:30 today, we received a report of an incident involving the use of a dangerous weapon," police spokesperson Jakub Filipiak told Reuters.
"One person was injured and transported to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Two other bystanders also sustained injuries but did not require hospitalisation."
He said the attacker was a 21-year-old student of the college.
State news agency PAP reported that the victims were two 17-year-old girls and a 24-year-old woman who had come to submit enrollment documents. Preliminary police findings indicated that the attacker and victims did not know one other, PAP reported.
Police said on Saturday they had inspected some 50,000 facilities since Friday and detained 76 people. Authorities had previously said most of the people detained were teenagers who had made threats online.
On Thursday, a 15-year-old former pupil wearing a helmet-mounted camera [USN:L8N45U0GO TEXT:"killed a caretaker"] and injured two teachers at a primary school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of Warsaw. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old [USN:L1N45T0N9 TEXT:"wounded 10 people"] including himself at a school in Ostroleka, north of the capital.

items.title: Rayo-Bilbao match abandoned after fans' protest against club owner
items.author: David Latona
items.creator: David Latona
items.summary: The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and rubber marbles into the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
items.body:
The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and rubber marbles into the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
The game was the first of this league season played at the Estadio de Vallecas, which was temporarily [USN:L1N43U0P3 TEXT:"closed"] after an audit found serious safety issues. Rayo fans blame negligence by club owner Raul Martin Presa, who in turn accused regional authorities of deliberately targeting his club.
The Sports Association of Rayo Vallecano fan group said in a statement after the suspension that their protest was "legitimate and democratic... necessary and peaceful", adding that it was the "consequence of three decades of putting the safety and health of 15,000 people at risk every fortnight".
La Liga said in a statement on social media that it "strongly condemned this type of behaviour, which endangers safety and makes the normal development of the competition impossible".
A new date and time for the match to take place will be announced shortly, LaLiga said.
Rayo, who reached the UEFA Conference League final in May, did not immediately reply to Reuters' request for comment.
After the first three home games were moved to the stadium of second division Leganes, registering some of La Liga's lowest-ever attendance figures, home fans started chanting, jeering and whistling against Presa before kickoff on Saturday.
By the 13th minute -- when Rayo ultras usually chant the song "Presa leave already" -- hundreds of fans launched paper planes and small rubber balls on to the pitch, prompting the referee to suspend play.
A 15-minute pause ensued, during which the stadium's speaker urged spectators not to throw objects on to the field as staff hastily removed them.
When play resumed a little later, fans in the south stand again hurled objects on to the grass and the referee abandoned the game.
Anger at Presa's management has [USN:L8N3NH005 TEXT:"reached boiling point"] in recent months, following the closure of Vallecas stadium for Rayo's opening home games of the season.
In a friendly against Cagliari last Saturday, anti-Presa graffiti appeared in the VIP box, which fans surrounded in protest before leaving the stadium.

A 15-minute pause ensued, during which the stadium's speaker urged spectators not to throw objects on to the field as staff hastily removed them.
When play resumed a little later, fans in the south stand again hurled objects on to the grass and the referee abandoned the game.
Anger at Presa's management has reached boiling point in recent months, following the closure of Vallecas stadium for Rayo's opening home games of the season.
In a friendly against Cagliari last Saturday, anti-Presa graffiti appeared in the VIP box, which fans surrounded in protest before leaving the stadium.

items.title: Several wounded in Riyadh airport attack, operations suspended, Saudi aviation authority says
items.author: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
items.summary: Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country's civil aviation authority said.
items.body:
Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country's civil aviation authority said.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, but it comes amid an escalation of [USN:L1N45V08F TEXT:"missile strikes"] by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia.
The airport had already been struck in two earlier attacks this week that left four people dead and exposed vulnerabilities in the kingdom's ability to defend itself as it wages war on the Houthis. Saudi Arabia's early warning system did not issue an alert ahead of Saturday's incident.
The Saudi government's media office did not immediately respond to questions from Reuters.
One eyewitness at the airport on Saturday reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing towards the facility.
An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.
US TO "LOOK AT" JOINING SAUDI FIGHT AGAINST HOUTHIS: TRUMP Following the attack, US President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, was asked whether the United States planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.
"We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," he said.
The US embassy in Riyadh said it was "aware of attacks" and "strongly recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas."
The UK and Irish embassies in Saudi Arabia said in statements on X that they were also aware of a "serious incident" at the airport. The Canadian embassy said that "ongoing military activity" had impacted operations at the airport.
RIYADH DUE TO HOLD MAJOR SUMMITS Flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point.
Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the closure of Riyadh airport because of the "security situation" there.
Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday.
Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"major energy and investment conferences"].
Organisers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.
The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.

items.title: Ronaldo, provisionalmente suspendido por abandono de la selección portuguesa, según medios
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo ha sido suspendido provisionalmente por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) tras la apertura de un expediente disciplinario por la marcha del delantero de la concentración de la selección nacional, informaron el sábado medios de comunicación portugueses.
items.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo ha sido suspendido provisionalmente por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) tras la apertura de un expediente disciplinario por la marcha del delantero de la concentración de la selección nacional, informaron el sábado medios de comunicación portugueses.
El jugador, de 41 años, abandonó la concentración del equipo en Copenhague antes del partido de la Liga de Naciones que Portugal disputó contra Dinamarca la semana pasada, tras una desavenencia con el seleccionador Jorge Jesús.
Ronaldo, que no llegó a salir al campo en el partido contra Noruega, acusó a Jesús de haber incumplido en dos ocasiones su palabra respecto a su papel en el equipo.
Según el periódico portugués A Bola, la FPF confirmó que se había abierto un expediente disciplinario.
"Sin perjuicio de la suspensión preventiva automática a la que estaba sujeto hasta la fecha de inicio del procedimiento, se dictó una suspensión preventiva no automática del jugador y se concedió carácter de urgencia al procedimiento", dijo la FPF, según el medio.
Ronaldo se disculpó el martes por no haber saludado a la afición tras el partido contra Noruega y por haber abandonado a sus compañeros de equipo, y añadió que seguiría estando disponible tras cumplir cualquier sanción derivada del incidente.
Reuters se puso en contacto con la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol para recabar sus comentarios.

items.title: UN Human Rights office condemns racist abuse targeting Gauff
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The United Nations Human Rights office has condemned online racist abuse faced by Coco Gauff after a replayed point sparked a backlash against the American tennis player this week.
items.body:
The United Nations Human Rights office has condemned online racist abuse faced by Coco Gauff after a replayed point [USN:L4N45S06O TEXT:"sparked a backlash"] against the American tennis player this week.
Gauff was targeted after stopping play during a crucial point in her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board as Sun was about to hit a winner.
The umpire ordered the point to be replayed after a video review, and Gauff went on to win the match 7-5 6-1, but the American later revealed in a social media post that she had received a huge amount of racist abuse following the match.
"You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff, who is Black, said on X in reply to a post containing a racial slur.
The official UN Human Rights office posted a statement on Saturday calling for players, coaches and sports bodies to unite against racial and sexist abuse.
"Racist messages such as those targeting tennis player Coco Gauff online are appalling and illustrate that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse," it wrote on X.
"There is no place in sport for racial or sexist slurs and abuse. Players, coaches, and sports bodies need to stand up for those facing such attacks and fans need to push back against those who sully sport with racism and sexism."
Reuters has contacted the WTA, the governing body of women's tennis, and tournament organisers in Beijing for comment.
Twice Grand Slam winner Gauff [USN:L1N45T0DY TEXT:"exited the tournament"] on Wednesday with a round-of-16 loss, and said the incident had left her drained.
A study by the WTA and World Tennis showed players were subjected to over 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025, up from 8,000 posts the previous year.

items.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended after national team walkout, media reports say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The 41-year-old left the squad's base in Copenhagen before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark last week, after a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus.
items.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the striker's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday.
The 41-year-old left the squad's base in [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"Copenhagen"] before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark last week, after a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo, an unused substitute against Norway, [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"accused Jesus"] of twice breaking his word regarding his role in the team.
According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, the FPF confirmed that disciplinary proceedings had been opened.
"Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status," the federation was quoted as saying.
Ronaldo apologised on Tuesday for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway game and for leaving his team mates, adding that he would remain available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.
Reuters has contacted the Portuguese Football Federation for comment.

items.title: Trump asegura que Putin suministrará diésel a EE.UU. antes de las elecciones de mitad de legislatura
items.author: Catherine Lucey, Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Will Kubzansky
items.summary: La medida ha suscitado críticas por parte del presidente de Ucrania, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, y de los aliados europeos, quienes afirman que no traerá la paz y que, por el contrario, permitirá a Rusia con ...
items.body: Bloomberg — El presidente Donald Trump está colaborando con Vladimir Putin para suministrar diésel ruso a los mercados mundiales, una medida que da un vuelco a años de sanciones, en un momento en que la Casa Blanca busca formas de frenar la escalada de los precios del combustible de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura en EE.UU. Ver más: México importa más diésel del que registra la Secretaría de Energía, según datos de EE.UU. Trump anunció el viernes una serie de envíos que comenzarán este mes y que ascenderán, en un primer momento, a unos 13,5 millones de barriles. El Kremlin publicó un comunicado en el que se citaba a Putin, quien afirmó que Rusia estaba dispuesta “a suministrar petróleo y productos petrolíferos a los mercados de EE.UU. y a los mercados mundiales”. El Tesoro de EE. UU. también concedió una exención para el combustible ruso que anteriormente estaba sujeto a sanciones. “Se trata de cantidades enormes de petróleo que llegan a nuestro país, y quiero dar las gracias al presidente Putin”, declaró Trump a los periodistas en la Casa Blanca el viernes. “Y es diésel, que es lo que queremos”. Tras el anuncio, los aliados europeos de Ucrania, entre ellos el Reino Unido y Alemania, reiteraron su apoyo a Kiev y a la continuidad de las sanciones contra Rusia. El diésel, el combustible al que a menudo se denomina “el motor de la economía mundial”, ha pasado a ocupar un lugar destacado en la actualidad, ya que una grave escasez de suministro ha disparado los precios en las gasolineras hasta niveles récord y ha avivado la preocupación por una inflación impulsada por los precios de la energía. De cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EE.UU. en noviembre, la Administración Trump está llevando a cabo una serie de medidas destinadas a reducir los precios, que han incrementado los costos para los agricultores y los camioneros. Sin embargo, la medida relativa a Rusia corre el riesgo de desencadenar una reacción geopolítica adversa sin aumentar la oferta lo suficiente como para reducir los precios de forma significativa. Los futuros del diésel estadounidense cayeron tras conocerse la noticia, cotizando en torno a los US$4,66 por galón, una cifra que sigue situándose en máximos históricos para esta época del año. Desde julio, Rusia ha operado bajo una prohibición autoimpuesta de exportación de diésel, tras meses de ataques devastadores contra sus refinerías por parte de drones ucranianos. Dichos ataques han continuado en los últimos días, pero Rusia está empezando a levantar sus restricciones a las exportaciones de gasóleo de forma inmediata, antes de lo previsto, según informó TASS citando a Alexander Novak, viceprimer ministro del país responsable de energía. El acuerdo entre Trump y Putin ha despertado la ira del presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Los ataques rusos contra Ucrania han causado decenas de víctimas mortales solo en los últimos días, según afirmó la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, en una publicación en X el viernes por la mañana. Kiev se ha visto afectada por cortes de electricidad, y los hospitales y colegios se encuentran entre los objetivos rusos. “Los regalos a Putin no traerán la paz ni ningún beneficio al mundo civilizado”, afirmó Zelenskyy en una publicación en X. “Rusia ‘devolverá’ el diésel con más terror y perfidia. Permitir que Rusia venda productos petrolíferos es una inversión en una guerra que hay que acabar, no prolongar”. Los aliados europeos se opusieron a esta medida. Alemania “sigue comprometida con las sanciones impuestas a Rusia y está trabajando con sus socios europeos en nuevas sanciones”, afirmó un portavoz del Gobierno federal alemán en un comunicado. “El apoyo a Ucrania en su lucha defensiva sigue siendo inquebrantable”. El Reino Unido afirmó que seguirá colaborando con sus socios internacionales para garantizar que Ucrania cuente con el apoyo militar y financiero que necesita para defenderse. El líder demócrata del Senado de EE.UU., Chuck Schumer, también criticó la decisión de Trump. “Trump está haciendo un pacto con el diablo para intentar salvar su tambaleante suerte política ante los precios escandalosamente altos del diésel”, afirmó Schumer en una publicación en X. Aunque el líder estadounidense ya había instado anteriormente a Ucrania a detener sus ataques contra la infraestructura petrolera rusa, el país, por el contrario, ha intensificado sus ataques contra los activos petroleros rusos en un intento por frenar la capacidad del Kremlin para financiar y mantener su guerra. “Ucrania no incendiará las refinerías de petróleo rusas si Rusia no destruye nuestra infraestructura energética. Este es el tipo de acuerdo que proponemos a Estados Unidos, y creemos que este país tiene poder suficiente para alcanzar dicho compromiso”, afirmó Zelenskyy. Un periodista le leyó a Trump los comentarios de Zelenskyy en la Casa Blanca, y el líder estadounidense respondió: “Somos un socio fuerte”. “Necesitamos petróleo para el mundo, y esto es diésel, que es lo que necesitamos. Así que estamos muy contentos de conseguirlo”, dijo Trump. Trump anunció una serie de entregas iniciales de producto, comenzando con 2,25 millones de barriles en octubre, 3,75 millones en noviembre y 7,5 millones “inmediatamente después”. Novak confirmó que Rusia está dispuesta a suministrar esa cantidad de combustible, con los 7,5 millones de barriles entregados en diciembre. Trump añadió que “en función del estado de sus refinerías de gasóleo, Rusia entregará entonces, en un breve plazo, 3 millones de toneladas de diésel” (lo que equivale a unos 22,5 millones de barriles). Existe preocupación sobre si la infraestructura energética rusa se encuentra en condiciones lo suficientemente sólidas como para cumplir esos objetivos, señaló Ryan McKay, estratega sénior de materias primas de TD Securities. “La mayor preocupación es que las refinerías sean capaces de hacerlo”, señaló McKay. Pero incluso si se liberaran los barriles prometidos, el impacto sería marginal, afirmó McKay. Esto es especialmente cierto en el caso de la liberación más inmediata, prevista para octubre, de tan solo 2,5 millones de barriles —alrededor del 10% de los barriles que Rusia exportaba al mes antes de que se intensificara la campaña en Ucrania—. “Esos barriles podrían ayudar, pero es posible que no se materialicen en su totalidad, y lo que llegue podría seguir siendo demasiado poco y llegar demasiado tarde”, señaló Rebecca Babin, operadora sénior de energía en CIBC Private Wealth Group. “La noticia puede influir en los precios inicialmente, pero difícilmente se trata de una solución sencilla”. Los precios minoristas del diésel en EE.UU. se situaban el jueves en US$6,28 el galón, por debajo de los máximos históricos de más de US6,50 registrados en septiembre. Zelenskyy ha intentado mantener a Trump de su lado mientras Rusia ha proseguido con sus ataques incesantes contra la infraestructura civil ucraniana. Los negociadores ucranianos tenían previsto reunirse el viernes en EE.UU. con los enviados estadounidenses Jared Kushner y Steve Witkoff. Trump afirmó el viernes que la liberación de las reservas rusas ayudaría a reducir los precios del diésel para los agricultores, ganaderos y camioneros estadounidenses —bloques de voto clave de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre, en las que el costo de la vida, incluido el de la energía, es el tema dominante—. Las encuestas muestran que Trump registra índices de aprobación en mínimos históricos y que los votantes están en gran medida decepcionados con su gestión de la economía y la guerra en Irán. El prolongado conflicto ha restringido los flujos de energía a través del estrecho de Ormuz, lo que ha elevado los precios del combustible a nivel mundial. Trump afirmó a principios de esta semana que no volvería a atacar Irán hasta después de las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre, lo que, según él, indicaba que las conversaciones con Teherán habían sido productivas. Mientras tanto, siguen vigentes otras restricciones globales sobre los suministros de combustible ruso. Antes de que se intensificaran los ataques de Ucrania esta primavera, la mayor parte de las exportaciones rusas por vía marítima se dirigían a Europa (excluida la Unión Europea), África, Asia y Brasil. Según datos de la Administración de Información Energética, la última vez que EE.UU. importó gasóleo de Rusia fue en marzo de 2022. El viernes, Trump no indicó si había abordado otros temas con Putin, como la reciente muerte de un trabajador de laboratorio en Siberia —que suscitó especulaciones sobre una plaga neumónica— o los recientes esfuerzos de EE.UU. por reactivar las conversaciones de paz para poner fin a la guerra del Kremlin en Ucrania. La agencia rusa Interfax informó el sábado de que Putin había transmitido a Trump las propuestas de Irán para una posible resolución del conflicto en Medio Oriente, en coordinación con el presidente iraní Masoud Pezeshkian, con quien Putin habló dos veces el jueves al margen de una cumbre celebrada en Turkmenistán. --Con la colaboración de Nick Wadhams, Yash Roy y Petra Sorge. items.title: Soccer-Guimaraes grabs winner as Arsenal rally to beat Leeds
items.author: Reuters

items.summary: Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
items.body:
Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
The competition returned under a cloud, with Manchester City found guilty by an independent commission of 100 breaches of the [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"league's financial rules"] over nine years as well as charges relating to their failure to co-operate with the investigation.
City have denied wrongdoing and said they will appeal against the decision.
On the pitch, champions Arsenal climbed to second in the table on 15 points, behind City on goal difference before the Manchester club travel to Liverpool on Sunday.
Chelsea struck twice in the opening three minutes en route to a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, with Jordan Henderson and Joao Pedro bagging two goals apiece, and are fifth on 10 points.
Brighton & Hove Albion moved into third place with a 2-0 win at Sunderland to move within two points of top spot.
Aston Villa and visiting Brentford drew 2-2, while Ipswich Town edged Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road with a last-gasp goal to leave the London side without a league victory this season.
Manchester United were hosting basement side Tottenham Hotspur in Saturday's late game.
FRUSTRATING FIRST HALF Arsenal were looking to bounce back, having slumped to a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in the last game before the break but endured a frustrating first half as they struggled to create chances.
Their play improved in the second period, but Leeds took the lead in the 55th minute when James Justin slammed home a clever pull-back from Gabriel Gudmundsson.
Riccardo Calafiori levelled for Arsenal seven minutes later, the Italian jumping to steer home Ben White's knock-down and, sensing his side could grab all three points, manager Mikel Arteta rang the changes.
He sent on Guimaraes, Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres, and was rewarded when Guimaraes grabbed the winner with a brilliantly worked goal in the 70th minute, sending a low shot into the far corner of the net from the edge of the box.
"It was such a difficult game, obviously after the international break it's never easy, especially after a defeat in our last game," Calafiori said.
"I think we had some tough moments, but I think we deserved the winner. We acted well after the goal we conceded."
Leeds are fifth on nine points.
UNLIKELY HERO At Stamford Bridge, Henderson was Chelsea's unlikely hero, opening the scoring in the second minute when Cole Palmer, fresh from signing a new contract, drove forward from the halfway line before setting him up to score.
Chelsea struck again a minute later when Henderson found Morgan Rogers, whose curling effort deflected in off defender Antonio Silva.
Chelsea extended their lead 40 seconds after halftime through Joao Pedro before Evanilson pulled one back for the visitors five minutes later. Joao Pedro netted the Blues' fourth before Henderson capped the win with a superb curling free kick.
Henderson, 36, became the oldest player to be directly involved in three-plus Premier League goals since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022.
Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scored in the second half for their side, whose victory came despite seeing Pascal Struijk red-carded in the 57th minute.
Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer struck in the 79th to salvage a draw at Villa that left his team fourth on 10 points. Yehor Yarmolyuk had opened the scoring for the visitors before Nicolas Jackson and John McGinn replied for Villa.
Ipswich captain Dara O'Shea scored in the 92nd minute to snatch victory over Fulham, who led through Ryan Sessegnon until the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara fired in a fine equaliser.

India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest

By Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Chaganti Singh and Sakshi Dayal
NEW DELHI, Oct 10 (Reuters) – Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and the founder of the “Cockroach” youth movement in Delhi on Saturday as security forces locked down parts of the capital to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India’s election chief.

Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended in the central business district and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a demonstration organised by the Cockroach movement.

The protest was aimed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Show Full Article

The movement had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi, but the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began.

A home ministry official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters more than 2,000 people were detained in Delhi. Local media said about 400 protesters were held in India’s financial hub, Mumbai.

There was no immediate comment from police on the detentions.

Small protests broke out elsewhere in Delhi, including at a popular crafts market and the memorial to freedom movement leader Mahatma Gandhi, with demonstrators demanding Kumar’s resignation.

“Long live the revolution,” some young protesters chanted as police chased them and dragged scores of others into buses to be taken away, even as more arrived, a Reuters witness said.

“This is violating the rights of the people and the country will not tolerate this anymore,” Yogendra Solanki told Reuters as police escorted him away.

MOVEMENT LEADERS HELD

Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka when their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi, the group said in a statement.

Television footage showed Dipke challenging officers who approached him on board the aircraft.

“I have come to be arrested, arrest me … I am not afraid of you guys,” he said.

“No, this is not an arrest,” one officer replied. “Please cooperate.”

The movement condemned what it called the “authoritarian detention” of its leaders, demanded their release and vowed to continue protesting.

“We will continue our protest tomorrow, day after … until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. We will be on the streets,” CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde told reporters.

CJP also said authorities refused to provide updates on the leaders’ whereabouts or health, even after news arrived of the death of Dipke’s grandmother. Police said Dipke was informed of her death and was offered help to return home for the funeral.

Some opposition lawmakers and former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee of West Bengal, Arvind Kejriwal of Delhi, and Pinarayi Vijayan of Kerala were also detained, TV channels showed.

Representatives of two digital news outlets said police briefly detained four of their reporters while they were covering the demonstrations. A Reuters journalist was also detained briefly before being released.

Across the capital of about 20 million people, security forces set up checkpoints on major roads and entry points, boarded buses searching for protesters and inspected vehicles. Barricades and concrete blocks disrupted traffic while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear-gas launchers guarded key routes.

NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI

The demonstrations represent one of the most serious tests yet for Modi, stemming from allegations that election authorities improperly revised voter rolls ahead of recent state polls.

Protests intensified after the Indian Express reported last week that two election commissioners had questioned Kumar’s voter-list revisions that removed roughly 130 million names from voter lists.

Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied allegations of wrongdoing.

The BJP says its electoral success reflects Modi’s popularity and India’s economic growth, and accuses opposition parties of spreading misinformation.

The near daily protests come just months after demonstrations over exam paper leaks forced his education minister to quit.

The unrest also comes ahead of a series of important state elections beginning in early 2027.

Rahul Gandhi, leader of the main opposition Congress party, said Modi’s opponents would not back down.

A senior BJP member, Ravi Shankar Prasad, said the party was not opposed to demonstrations but the street protests had been “weaponised” by rivals due to election defeats.

DELETIONS AFFECTED STATE POLLS, OPPOSITION ALLEGES

Opposition parties say the deletions affected the outcome of recent state elections won by the BJP and have cast a shadow over voting in the world’s largest democracy.

Election Commission data show about 130 million voter entries were removed during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated, 30 million who could not be traced and 28 million who had died.

The commission says the removals relate to entries identified during the draft revision process and that any eligible voter incorrectly deleted can re-enrol.

(Reporting by Saurabh Sharma, Aftab Ahmed, Sarita Chaganti Singh, Shanima A and Sakshi Dayal; Writing by YP Rajesh; Editing by Clarence Fernandez and Ros Russell)

RAMALLAH, Oct 10 (Reuters) – Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.

Abbas’ decree cited “obstacles posed by Israeli measures” to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for “free, fair and inclusive elections”. It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to participate in the polls.

There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead in late November. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas’ rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.

Show Full Article

The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel’s continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.

In Gaza, the decree pointed to “exceptional security and humanitarian conditions”, the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.

Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.

The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation’s executive committee and consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process.

(Reporting by Ali Sawafta in Ramallah, Nidal Al-Mughrabi in Cairo and Eman Abouhassira in Dubai, Editing by Alexandra Hudson)

items.title: Spanish lawyer Gonzalez Durantez launches centrist party for November election
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an early general election on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions.
items.body:
Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an [USN:L1N45V07B TEXT:"early general election"] on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions.
Gonzalez Durantez, who is married to former British Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg and specialises in international and EU trade law, said the party, called Democracy21, will run in the election in Madrid and Barcelona.
The party enters a volatile political landscape after Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the snap election on Monday following parliament's rejection of measures to address a [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"mounting housing crisis"]. Opinion polls point to the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox likely winning a combined parliamentary majority.
Referring to the left-right political divide in Spain exemplified by the deep rivalry between the Socialists and the PP, she criticised "two rigid blocs with nothing to foster consensus".
Gonzalez Durantez called on Spaniards to "set aside our ideological differences, to stand united, and to work together to safeguard democracy and modernise the country."
The crisis has triggered continuing mass protests over home shortages and surging rents, stoked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, whose death on Tuesday further angered protesters.
Gonzalez Durantez blamed both the ruling coalition and the opposition, which controls most of Spain's regions, for the housing crisis, calling their politicians "a cost, a burden for the country" who expressly failed to develop and urbanise the land.
"They haven't used the permits to build housing; instead, they've used them to line the coffers of their city councils. They've imposed so many regulations, many of them absurd, that they've doubled the price per square meter of construction and have made it almost impossible for us to build affordable housing," she told supporters.
Central government can set housing legislation and devise nationwide plans for incentives and subsidies, but their implementation, and wider urban planning, is largely devolved to regional governments and municipalities.
She said she would identify a problem and not play politics with it. "I won’t use it to pit one group against another, no, I’ll simply fix it."

items.title: Home favourite Zheng sets up China Open final against Andreeva
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.
items.body:
French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.
Zheng, who received a wildcard entry to the tournament after recovering from an elbow injury, became the first Chinese player to reach the final in Beijing as she outplayed Belgian 13th seed Mertens 7-5 6-2 after Andreeva crushed Bartunkova 6-2 6-2.
Zheng made an early break to build a 4-2 lead, but made a number of errors to hand Mertens the break back.
But the 24-year-old, who is chasing her first WTA 1000 title on home soil, remained calm to build a 6-5 lead, before her strong crosscourt forehand earned her another break point which she converted when Mertens netted.
Zheng dominated the second set to secure her second clash with Andreeva, having beaten the Russian when they met in the 2024 Beijing quarter-finals.
"I always want to give my best here. It's like the fifth Grand Slam for me," said Zheng, who reached the semi-final in 2024.
In the first semi-final, Andreeva took an hour and 14 minutes to beat Bartunkova and reach her second WTA 1000 final of the year.
Czech Bartunkova committed 20 unforced errors, twice as many as Andreeva, as the world number five hit 27 winners to clinch victory.
Andreeva is relishing her first China Open final.
"Of course, we all know that (Zheng) is playing at home. That's okay. Also, she's been coming back, she's been playing better, she's been beating a lot of great players," the 19-year-old told reporters.

items.title: Neither Putin nor Trump wanted to hang up first, Kremlin aide says after 'very friendly' call
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.
items.body:
A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.
During the call, the presidents agreed that Russia would [USN:FWN45V0WZ TEXT:"supply diesel"] to the US and global markets to lower fuel prices, prompting an unexpected temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian fuel that has [USN:L1N45V0WX TEXT:"dismayed"] Ukraine.
The Kremlin said most of the conversation focused on efforts to resolve the war in Ukraine . Putin also [USN:L1N45V0ZL TEXT:"downplayed"] the likelihood of three-way peace talks resuming soon.
Interfax cited Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov on Saturday as saying the conversation lasted an hour and a half.
"Neither wanted to be the first to hang up," he said. "They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time."
Kyiv is relying on US support in negotiations to end the war. After news of the call broke on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:L1N45V0WX TEXT:"condemned"] the diesel deal in unusually blunt terms, calling it a "weak decision" and "an investment in a war that must be ended."
The West imposed sanctions, including restrictions on Russian energy imports, after Moscow launched the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Efforts to end the fighting have so far stalled, partly over Russia’s demand for four Ukrainian regions it does not fully control.
On Friday, negotiators from the US, Ukraine and European countries [USN:L1N45V11A TEXT:"held talks"] in Miami aimed at reaching agreement on a unified peace proposal in the coming weeks that could be presented to Russia, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
items.raw_description: A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.

items.title: Palmer firma un contrato con el Chelsea hasta 2034
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League.
items.body:
El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League.
El internacional inglés, de 24 años, se ha convertido en una figura clave desde que llegó al Chelsea procedente del Manchester City en 2023, con un registro de 91 goles en 138 partidos en todas las competiciones.
Formó parte de la plantilla que ganó el Mundial de Clubes y la UEFA Conference League.
"Hablé con los propietarios, con los directores deportivos y, por supuesto, con el entrenador, y me transmitieron mucha confianza, así que lo lógico era firmar", dijo Palmer.
"Al hablar también con los jugadores, veo que todos comparten las mismas ambiciones. Tengo la sensación de que aquí ganaremos grandes títulos constantemente".
El Chelsea ha acordado contratos a largo plazo con varios jugadores del primer equipo y con jóvenes promesas.
El delantero João Pedro firmó recientemente un contrato hasta 2034, y el extremo Pedro Neto acordó el mes pasado un contrato de seis años.

items.title: La presidencia irlandesa de la UE quiere un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto para 2028-2034
items.author: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
items.creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
items.summary: La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente.
items.body:
La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente.
La propuesta irlandesa supone, a pesar de todo, un aumento del 30% respecto del presupuesto actual del bloque, que abarca el periodo de 2021 a 2027. El presupuesto de la UE es la principal fuente de financiación de todas las políticas fundamentales del bloque de 27 países.
La Comisión, el órgano ejecutivo de la UE, ha señalado que el bloque debe destinar más fondos a la defensa y al impulso de la competitividad europea, mientras que algunos Estados miembros desean mantener la mayor parte del gasto destinado al apoyo a la agricultura y al desarrollo regional.
"La 'caja de negociación' supone un ahorro del 8%, es decir, 141.000 millones de euros, respecto a la propuesta original de la Comisión", dijo Irlanda, que actualmente y por seis meses preside la UE, refiriéndose a su propuesta de compromiso.
Irlanda ajustó la cifra original de la Comisión, de 2 billones de euros, teniendo en cuenta la inflación en siete años, situándola en 1,76 billones de euros a precios de 2025, lo que supuso una reducción del 8%.
"Tal y como lo vemos, el marco de negociación sirve para salvar las numerosas diferencias entre los Estados miembros", dijo el ministro irlandés Thomas Byrne en una rueda de prensa.
"Nos acerca a la resolución del trilema presupuestario, abordando las conversaciones sobre la mejor forma de financiar nuevas prioridades en materia de competitividad, investigación, innovación, seguridad y defensa, al tiempo que se abordan las políticas fundamentales", añadió.
La propuesta establece un recorte del 3% del gasto en desarrollo regional, agricultura y pesca respecto de las propias cifras de la Comisión —la partida más importante del presupuesto— y una reducción del 13% en el gasto en competitividad y seguridad.
Los líderes de la UE debatirán la propuesta irlandesa en Bruselas el 15 y 16 de octubre. El presupuesto de la UE, conocido como Marco Financiero Plurianual, debe ser aprobado por los 27 Estados miembros.
(1 dólar = 0,8928 euros)

items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
items.author: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
items.body:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, pointing to the last Palestinian election having been held two decades ago, rejected Abbas' remarks as "yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability."
There had been serious doubts that the [USN:L8N45G1M5 TEXT:"Palestinian Authority vote"] would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-2006, after which Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009.
The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November.
In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize.
The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process.
PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday to postpone the elections.
An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research (PSR) showed declining support for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions.
The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms.
Abbas had committed in writing to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025.
France's foreign ministry [USN:L1N45V090 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that holding the elections was essential, and it welcomed the launch of an EU election observation mission.

items.title: Report à 2027 des élections palestiniennes
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA.
items.body:
Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA.
Le décret de Mahmoud Abbas évoque les "obstacles créés par les mesures israéliennes" à la tenue des élections en novembre ainsi que la nécessité de réunir des conditions politiques, sécuritaires et de terrain adaptées à l'organisation d'"élections libres, équitables et inclusives".
Il appelle les Palestiniens de Jérusalem, de Cisjordanie et de Gaza à participer au scrutin.
De sérieux doutes existaient quant à la tenue du scrutin de l'Autorité palestinienne à la fin novembre. Les Palestiniens n'ont plus organisé d'élections législatives ni présidentielle depuis 2005-2006, à l'issue desquelles le Hamas, rival islamiste du président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas, a pris le contrôle de Gaza en évinçant ses partisans.
Le décret précise que les attaques militaires israéliennes, l'expansion des colonies, les violences de colons et les restrictions de circulation en Cisjordanie, y compris à Jérusalem-Est, ainsi que la poursuite du gel par Israël des recettes fiscales palestiniennes, ont créé des difficultés pour préparer et organiser les élections à la date initialement prévue.
À Gaza, le décret fait état de "conditions sécuritaires et humanitaires exceptionnelles", du retrait inachevé des forces israéliennes, de l'absence de progrès dans la reconstruction et de la non-mise en oeuvre des dispositions relatives au déploiement de forces internationales de stabilisation et de police.
Les restrictions imposées par Israël à l'accès de Gaza et de Jérusalem-Est pour les personnels de la commission électorale et les observateurs internationaux ont également compliqué les préparatifs, ajoute le décret.
La décision de report fait suite à une résolution du comité exécutif de l'Organisation de libération de la Palestine (OLP) et à des consultations avec les factions palestiniennes et les forces politiques. Elle vise également à laisser le temps nécessaire à un dialogue national palestinien global afin de renforcer l'unité et de répondre aux défis auxquels est confronté le processus électoral.

items.title: Eritrea asks UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war".
items.body:
Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war".
The [USN:L6N45T121 TEXT:"incursion by Eritrean troops"], which [USN:L8N45Q06L TEXT:"Asmara has denied"] and Reuters could not independently verify, has raised fears of a return to [USN:L6N45M0WY TEXT:"all-out war"] along Ethiopia's northern border where the two Horn of Africa neighbours have clashed before.
Conflicts elsewhere in the region and tensions across the Red Sea have further raised the stakes.
Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said in the letter that the incursion claims were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression. He urged the UN to intervene.
"Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia's deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea ... and take the requisite deterrent measures against it in accordance with Chapter VII of the UN Charter," he wrote.
Chapter VII allows for measures ranging from sanctions to military action, though Osman did not specify what measures Eritrea was calling for.
Ethiopia itself [USN:L8N45V0CC TEXT:"wrote to Security Council members"] on Friday, stating that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km (37 miles) inside the northern region of Tigray in recent days. It warned that the presence of foreign troops left Addis Ababa with no option but to defend itself.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Saturday.
ETHIOPIAN TROOPS, MILITIA ALLIES MOVE INTO TIGRAYAN CITY Earlier in the day, Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered the Tigrayan city of Adigrat, near the border with Eritrea, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops [USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"were "][USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"pushed back"] from the strategic city.
A video shared on social media and verified by Reuters showed members of a militia allied with the Ethiopian government walking in the streets of Adigrat, which is located 30 km (19 miles) from the border with Eritrea.
Three Adigrat residents also told Reuters they had seen the Ethiopian army and an allied militia in the city on Saturday morning, with one of the residents saying they saw soldiers on patrol along with military vehicles.
Explosions were reported on Wednesday and Thursday near Adigrat, as the US-based conflict monitor ACLED said Ethiopia used drone strikes against Eritrean forces, who then withdrew from positions near the city.
The explosions continued on Friday, according to an Adigrat resident, who told Reuters they had heard repeated explosions overnight and into the morning several kilometres outside town.
ETHIOPIAN SEA ACCESS A FLASH POINT Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said on Friday that Eritrea had shown restraint. He said a 2023 statement by landlocked Ethiopia that it would acquire sovereign access to the sea amounted to declaring a war of aggression against his country.
Ethiopia had access to a coastline for decades until Eritrea gained independence from Addis Ababa in 1993. Ethiopia argues that restoring sea access is an existential issue but has said it would be restored through peace and dialogue.
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing the rebel alliance that has been battling government troops since September 23 in its northern regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Eritrea has denied doing so.
After years of war, Eritrea and Ethiopia made peace in a 2018 agreement that earned Ethiopia's Abiy the Nobel Peace Prize. Eritrea fought in support of Ethiopia’s federal government during a 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray, but relations soured again toward the end of that conflict.
The fighting that broke out last month has been the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war, in which hundreds of thousands died.

items.title: Ukraine-Une attaque russe fait 20 morts à Zaporijjia, passe d'armes Zelensky-Trump
items.author: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
items.creator: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
items.summary: Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv.
items.body:
Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv.
Une fillette de six ans figure parmi les victimes d'une frappe qui a réduit une partie d'un immeuble résidentiel à l'état de gravats.
Dix-huit autres personnes ont été blessées dans cette attaque contre Zaporijjia, ville industrielle dont la périphérie se situe à moins de 30 km de la ligne de front.
"Aujourd'hui, la Russie a fêté la levée des sanctions sur les exportations de diesel en larguant cinq bombes planantes sur des immeubles résidentiels à Zaporijjia", a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky, dans l'une de ses critiques les plus virulentes à ce jour à l'encontre de la Maison blanche.
Donald Trump a rétorqué que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement" de bombarder les raffineries russes, ajoutant : "Je suggère qu'ils (les Ukrainiens, NDLR) se trouvent un nouveau dirigeant capable de conclure un accord."
L'attaque russe de samedi est la dernière en date d'une série de frappes particulièrement meurtrières en Ukraine ces dernières semaines. Près de 80 civils ont été tués lors de frappes russes mercredi et jeudi, dont au moins 30 dans un bombardement contre la ville-garnison de Kramatorsk, dans l'est du pays, et 22 autres dans une attaque de missile contre la ville de Pryluky, située à environ 130 km à l'est de Kyiv.
Le gouverneur local, Mykhaïlo Semikine, a déclaré que la Russie avait frappé plusieurs sites simultanément dans les premières heures de samedi.
Des secouristes ont progressé à travers les décombres pour extraire vivants d'autres habitants de l'immeuble. Un homme, dont la jambe était coincée sous les gravats, criait de douleur pendant qu'il était dégagé.
"D'AUTRES SIGNAUX SONT NÉCESSAIRES" Zaporijjia, qui comptait plus de 700.000 habitants avant la guerre, est régulièrement visée par les bombardements russes, dont l'intensité s'est accrue au cours des derniers mois.
"La nuit dernière a constitué une nouvelle confirmation que la Russie considère tout allègement de la pression comme un signal lui permettant soi-disant de continuer à faire la guerre, de continuer à larguer des bombes sur les villes. D'autres signaux sont nécessaires", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky.
Une attaque de missile menée samedi après-midi a également frappé un restaurant à Kyiv, blessant sept personnes.
Des drones russes ont survolé la capitale ukrainienne tout au long de la journée dans le cadre d'une nouvelle vague massive de bombardements, la plus importante depuis les premiers jours de la guerre.
Le ministère russe de la Défense a déclaré samedi en début se soirée que ses drones avaient frappé plus tôt un centre de traitement de données à Kyiv ainsi qu'un cargo transportant des fournitures militaires vers le port ukrainien d'Odessa.
Dans un communiqué, il a ajouté que le site de Kyiv était utilisé par les forces armées ukrainiennes pour collecter, traiter et stocker des renseignements. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations dans l'immédiat.
La décision de Donald Trump de lever les sanctions sur les exportations de diesel russe intervient alors que son administration cherche à enrayer la hausse des prix des carburants, qui ont bondi dans le contexte du conflit opposant les États-Unis à l'Iran.
Kyiv avait au contraire exhorté Washington à accroître la pression sur la Russie afin de la contraindre à engager de véritables négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre, qui dure depuis quatre ans et demi.
L'ACCORD SUR LE DIESEL A PRIS KYIV PAR SURPRISE Donald Trump a en outre critiqué les frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes, estimant qu'elles avaient contribué à faire grimper les prix mondiaux. Kyiv dit vouloir un arrêt total des attaques visant les infrastructures énergétiques des deux camps, alors que Moscou continue de pilonner le réseau électrique ukrainien.
Samedi, plusieurs secteurs de Kyiv et de sa région ont été privés d'électricité, provoquant l'arrêt complet du métro de la capitale pour la deuxième fois de la semaine.
Ces dernières frappes sont intervenues après des discussions à Miami entre responsables ukrainiens et européens et négociateurs américains, vendredi, en vue d'élaborer une proposition commune pour mettre fin à la guerre, selon une source proche du dossier.
L'agence de presse officielle russe Tass, citant une source, a rapporté samedi que les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner pourraient se rendre à Moscou au cours des deux prochaines semaines.
Donald Trump a annoncé l'accord sur le diesel alors que les négociations de vendredi étaient en cours, une décision qui, selon Volodimir Zelensky, a pris Kyiv par surprise.
Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré, à l'issue d'un entretien téléphonique avec son homologue américain, qu'une reprise immédiate des pourparlers de paix était peu probable, invoquant les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre Moscou.
Par ailleurs, quatre civils ont été tués et cinq autres blessés à la suite d'attaques ukrainiennes contre la région de Louhansk, sous contrôle russe dans l'est de l'Ukraine, a déclaré samedi le gouverneur local installé par Moscou.
Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier cette information de manière indépendante et l'Ukraine n'a pas fait de commentaire dans l'immédiat.

items.title: Riders stage safety protest before start of Giro di Lombardia
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Riders at the Giro di Lombardia staged a five-minute protest before the start of Saturday's race to highlight growing safety concerns following a series of incidents involving race vehicles, the tournament organisers said.
items.body:
Riders at the Giro di Lombardia staged a five-minute protest before the start of Saturday's race to highlight growing safety concerns following a series of incidents involving race vehicles, the tournament organisers said.
The protest came days after riders Thomas Gloag and Marcel Camprubi were struck by a police motorcycle travelling in the opposite direction during Tre Valli Varesine.
"At the start of Il Lombardia, the riders came together to send an important message, stopping for five minutes to urge all road users to behave responsibly and show mutual respect, both during races and in everyday life," organisers RCS Sport said in a social media post.
After organisers completed the start countdown, the peloton remained stationary, before Belgium's double Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel stepped forward to explain the riders' action.
"There’s too many incidents happening with vehicles in the race," Evenepoel said.
"Unfortunately we lost the life of a brother and of a colleague of us, so we want to make this statement to show to the world that we cannot keep accepting the fact that guys are getting injured or literally dying in what we like the most to do."
Evenepoel was referring to the death of British cyclist Finlay [USN:L4N44B13Q TEXT:"Tarling"], younger brother of Ineos rider Josh Tarling, who was killed in a collision with a vehicle during the Tour of Portugal on August 14.
The demonstration delayed the start of the final Monument race of the season by five minutes before the peleton set off.
Reuters has contacted the International Cycling Union (UCI) for comment.

items.title: Philips wins Dutch court battle with shareholders over recall
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A Dutch court on Saturday dismissed demands by shareholders of health technology company Philips for an investigation into allegations of misleading disclosures and management failures linked to the company's recall of sleep apnea devices.
items.body:
A Dutch court on Saturday dismissed demands by shareholders of health technology company Philips (PHG.AS) for an investigation into allegations of misleading disclosures and management failures linked to the company's recall of sleep apnea devices.
A large group of shareholders had [USN:L5N3VB062 TEXT:"demanded"] a court inquiry, as they said Philips executives had responded too late to the problems that led to the massive recall and had failed to adequately inform investors.
Philips' shares lost about two thirds of their value when the company recalled around 15 million sleep apnea devices in 2021, after discovering that the foam in the machines could release harmful substances and might pose health risks.
The Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal in its ruling said it had found no indication that Philips had known about the problems long before it issued any warning.
It also said there was no reason to assume executives should have intervened earlier at the Respironics subsidiary that made the devices.
Philips had denied the accusations made by the shareholders and said it welcomed the court's decision.
The sleep apnea devices recall led to probes in multiple countries, including France, where prosecutors are still investigating charges of aggravated fraud and failure to report safety risks.
Philips in 2024 agreed to pay $1.1 billion to settle all personal injury claims related to the devices filed in the US.
